summary: Feed s067_single is degraded: 36.3% of TCP sessions (62/171) are one-way, so IDS lacks return traffic for stateful analysis. All other visibility checks (duplicates, encryption, VLAN, drops, overload, truncation, tunnels, oversize) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker / SPAN is forwarding only one direction of bidirectional flows to this single tool port. 62 of 171 TCP sessions show traffic in only one direction (36.3% > 10% threshold), consistent with a SPAN/mirror configured for Tx or Rx only, a broker filter/policy forwarding a single direction, or asymmetric routing without proper aggregation to the same IDS port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP state tracking, stream reassembly, and request/response signature matching. With only one side visible, the IDS cannot build full sessions, will miss exploits that span both directions, generates incomplete flows and reduces detection coverage significantly.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions (client->server and server->client) of each flow to the same IDS tool port and use symmetric hashing if load-balancing. If sourced from SPAN, verify SPAN includes both Tx and Rx or preferably replace with TAP aggregation to guarantee complete bidirectional visibility.
